ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a large square, which is first divided into four identical small squares; the small square in the upper left is shaded black. The small square in the lower right is again divided into four even smaller squares, among which the upper left is shaded black again; this lower-right recursive division and shading process continues infinitely toward the lower-right corner. Reasoning: The area of the original square is 84. It is first divided into four identical squares, so the area shaded black the first time is 84/4 = 21. The next time is in that piece in the lower right, which is again divided into four equal parts, and the shaded black area is 1/16 of the original area, namely 84/16 = 21/4. Continuing, the black areas are successively 84/4, 84/16, 84/64, ..., which is an infinite geometric sequence with first term 21 and common ratio 1/4. The total black area is 21/(1 - 1/4) = 21/(3/4) = 28.

method.method_draft: Identify from the diagram and text that each stage takes the lower-right square from the previous stage, divides it into 4 congruent squares, and colors the upper-left one black. The original square has area 84, so the first black square has area 84/4 = 21. The next black square is inside the lower-right quarter, so its area is 84/16 = 21/4. Continuing gives black areas 84/4, 84/16, 84/64, ... . Sum the infinite geometric series with first term 21 and ratio 1/4: total = 21/(1 - 1/4) = 28.
